The SOCKS5 client in subsys/net/lib/socks/socks.c built the CONNECT request in socks5_tcp_connect() by choosing the SOCKS5 address type from the address family of the proxy (proxy->sa_family) while reading the bytes out of the destination address supplied to connect(). A SOCKS5 request encodes the destination independently of the transport used to reach the proxy, so the two families are unrelated and nothing in the path forces them to agree: set_context_proxy() only requires the proxy family to match the socket, and zsock_connect_ctx() enters the SOCKS branch before any destination validation

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability to bypass manifest signature validation, potentially leading to execution of unauthorized code with elevated privileges.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an External Control of System or Configuration Setting vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of Privileges.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Untrusted Search Path vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of privilege.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Insecure Inherited Permissions vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized file operations with elevated privileges.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3 contain an Improper Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of Privilege.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain a Missing Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with physical access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information tampering.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Protection mechanism bypass.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3 contain a Download of Code Without Integrity Check vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code execution.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain a Download of Code Without Integrity Check vulnerability. A highly privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code execution.

Bludit through 3.22.0 contains an improper session invalidation vulnerability that allows demoted users to retain revoked privileges because Login::isLogged() never re-reads the session-stored role. Attackers holding a session issued while their account was an administrator can keep using it after demotion to perform administrator actions such as creating new administrator accounts.

Bludit through 3.22.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to modify the site logo by calling unprotected AJAX endpoints. Attackers with Author or Editor roles can send requests to logo-upload.php or logo-remove.php under /admin/ajax/ to replace the site logo with an uploaded image or delete it.

Kiwi TCMS is an open source test management system. From 16.1 until 16.2, the account confirmation page’s incomplete validation of the next parameter accepts protocol-relative URLs because the version 16.1 fix for CVE-2026-54724 only requires the value to start with a slash. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a confirmation URL on a trusted Kiwi TCMS hostname that redirects a user to an external site, enabling phishing and related downstream confidentiality or integrity impacts when the user follows the link. This issue is fixed in version 16.2.

tac_plus-ng before commit d8493e0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows clients holding the TACACS+ shared key to overflow a stack buffer due to an operator precedence error in author_pak_looks_bogus() and accounting_pak_looks_bogus(). Attackers can send packets whose argument-length table exceeds the payload, causing eval_args() to read past the packet and memcpy() oversized cmd values into cmdline, crashing the daemon or executing code.

Seerr before 3.5.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust disk space through unnormalized /imageproxy cache keys. Attackers can request the same TMDB image using many equivalent dot-segment path spellings, storing unlimited duplicate copies that fill the shared SQLite configuration volume and break logins and requests.

ep3-bs through 1.9.1b contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows staff users with only user management privilege to delete administrator accounts. Authenticated assistant accounts can invoke the backend UserController deleteAction against administrator targets to remove or mark them deleted, locking administrators out.

Pytition before 2.10 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the show_signatures view that allows registered users to delete other petitions' signatures by supplying foreign signature IDs. Attackers can post sequential signature IDs to their own petition's signatures page to permanently delete signatures from any user-owned petition and trigger confirmation emails to other signers.

linkdotnet Blog through 17.1 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by passing unvalidated redirectUri values on the Login and Logout pages. Attackers can craft login links sending victims to attacker-controlled sites after authentication, and inject persistent returnTo destinations into other users' logout redirects via the shared AuthInformation instance.

ClearFlask before 2.7.3 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows any account holding an invitation ID to accept it regardless of invited email. Attackers who obtain a forwarded or shared invitation link can redeem it via accountAcceptInvitationAdmin or accountSignupAdmin to become project administrators.

Ruby Central cfp-app through 2.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in CommentsController#create that allows any authenticated user to comment on any proposal by supplying a numeric proposal_id. Attackers can send POST requests to /public_comments or /internal_comments to post into reviewers' private discussions and trigger notifications to event team members.

GreaterWMS through 2.1.54 contains a predictable authentication token vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge openid tokens by recomputing an unsalted MD5 hash of username and registration timestamp. Attackers who know a username and can bound its registration time can brute-force candidate openid values in the Token header to gain full read and write access to warehouse, staff, customer, supplier and order data.

GreaterWMS through 2.1.54 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the css, js, statics and fonts routes in greaterwms/views.py, which concatenate raw request.path_info without normalization. Attackers can send URL-encoded ../ sequences to read db.sqlite3 and obtain user openid tokens, enabling impersonation of any account.

Pastefy 7.2.1 before 7.2.7 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in MermaidViewer.vue that passes attacker-supplied %%{init}%% directives to mermaid.mermaidAPI.updateSiteConfig(). Unauthenticated attackers can create Mermaid or Markdown pastes setting securityLevel to loose with a permissive dompurifyConfig to steal viewers' API session keys and act on their accounts.

wireguard_webadmin before 0.9981 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in scheduler/views.py that allows low-privilege authenticated users to manage peer schedules without Peer Manager level. View Only or Debugging Analyst users can create, modify, and delete schedule profiles and time slots to disable WireGuard peers or keep disabled peers off.

Coyote before commit d6e8fb9 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Wiki\CommentController::save that allows authenticated users to edit other users' wiki comments. Attackers can send POST requests to /Comment/Save/{wiki}/{id} with another user's comment id, bypassing the WikiCommentPolicy update check, so altered text appears under the original author's name.

ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the IAM role management API that allows authenticated tenant members to escalate privileges. Attackers holding even the lowest built-in role can call the permissions/grant-ids, permissions/grant, or bind/member routes to grant permissions or bind privileged roles, gaining tenant administrative access.

BeikeShop through 2.0.0.32 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered customers to inject script by submitting an unsanitized RMA comment rendered unescaped in mail templates. Attackers can submit a return request with malicious script saved to mail_logs.content, executing in an administrator's browser session when they view the Mail Logs entry.

UrlHub before 1.20.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to create accounts via the POST /admin/user/store route because role:admin middleware only covers view and create actions. Attackers, including self-registered users, can submit a request with role=admin to create an administrator account and gain full administrative control.

Flagr before 1.2.5 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access the flag management write API through an insecure default FLAGR_BASIC_AUTH_WHITELIST_PATHS including /api/v1/flags. Because basicAuth.whitelist() in pkg/config/middleware.go matches only path prefixes regardless of HTTP method, attackers can create, modify, enable, disable, and delete flags, variants, segments, constraints, and distributions.

Habitat through 1.7.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CreatePostController::addAttachmentsToPost() that allows authenticated users to claim other users' unposted image uploads. Email-verified attackers can submit sequential attachmentIds when creating a post to attach another user's pending image, exposing it publicly and removing it from the uploader's post.

FS PBX through 2.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in FaxesController, PaymentGatewayController and VirtualReceptionistController API routes that only check authentication. Any authenticated user can delete other tenants' fax records by UUID, deactivate or modify the platform-wide payment gateway, and change another tenant's IVR greeting.

EveryDocs Core before 1.6.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other users' records through unscoped Model.find(params[:id]) lookups in multiple controllers. Self-registered attackers can enumerate sequential ids to read, modify, or delete other users' documents and stored files, and rename or delete their folders, tags and people.

53AIHub before 0.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to reinitialize installed instances by calling the public POST /api/init endpoint. Attackers can reset an existing account's password, assign the top creator role, and obtain an access token to take over accounts and use admin-only API routes.

Bonsai through 6.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to access admin pages because AdminAuthHandler accepts both Administrator and Editor roles. Attackers can use UsersController and DynamicConfigController to reset administrator passwords, promote accounts to Administrator, and change global settings to take over the instance.

AudioBookRequest 1.9.0 through 2.0.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject script through manual book request fields due to disabled Jinja2 autoescaping. Attackers can submit malicious title, author, narrator or info values via POST /api/requests/manual to execute script in an administrator's browser and access admin-only endpoints.

Nexterm through 1.2.2-BETA contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows users with permissions.manage to gain unauthorized permissions because addGroupMember and setUserGroups lack the grantsBeyondCaller check. Attackers can add their own account to custom groups via the group membership endpoints to inherit permissions like users.impersonate and settings.backup.

wishthis through 1.2.3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the PUT branch of src/api/wishes.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify wish URLs across all users. Attackers who know a wish link from a public wishlist can supply wish_url_current and wish_url_proposed parameters to redirect owners and gift-givers to attacker-controlled URLs.

wishthis through 1.2.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in User::ownsWishlist() that allows authenticated users to modify other users' wishes and wishlists. Attackers can supply sequential wish_id and wishlist_id values to the wishes and wishlists API handlers to edit wishes, add wishes, or rename and delete wishlists.

LaraCollab through 0.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated client-role users to inject script by posting unsanitized task comments rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Attackers can post malicious comments that execute when users, including administrators, open the task or view dashboard recent comments, allowing actions in their session.

BZFlag bzfs before 2.4.32 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in NetHandler::tcpReceive() that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a TCP message with a body length of exactly 1024. Attackers can overwrite the tcplen receive offset with a negative value to write controlled bytes before the buffer, crashing the server or executing commands as the bzfs user.

Dolibarr ERP CRM through 24.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability in Website::importWebSite() that allows website editors without PHP permission to execute code by importing templates. Attackers can import a template zip whose javascript.js.php contains PHP code, which the public javascript.js.php endpoint includes, executing code as the web server user.

Dolibarr ERP CRM before 24.0.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the Users REST API put() method that allows non-admin API users to set administrator passwords. Authenticated users with user modification and password rights can send a PUT request to the users endpoint with a chosen pass value for a SuperAdmin account and then log in as that administrator.

AppFlowy-Web before 0.20.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the TextareaAutosize component that allows workspace members with edit access to inject markup by copying unescaped values into a hidden mirror via innerHTML. Attackers can store a database row title or checklist task containing an element with an event handler to execute script in browsers of users opening the row, including unauthenticated published page visitors.

CodeIgniter4 before 4.7.5 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the View Parser (system/View/Parser.php) that allows attackers to bypass auto-escaping through re-scanned substitutions. Attackers controlling one rendered value can inject Parser syntax like {other|raw} or {!other!} to emit unescaped attacker-controlled values, executing scripts in viewers' browsers.

HyperFrames before 0.8.216 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the engine URL downloader because isBlockedHost() only checks IP literals and never resolves DNS host names. Attackers can supply compositions with remote media, image or font URLs whose host names resolve to private addresses, making preview or render processes send HTTPS requests to internal services.

HyperFrames before 0.9.30 contains a missing Origin and Host validation vulnerability in the unauthenticated Studio API that allows malicious web pages to write project files. Attackers can send CORS-simple POST requests to /api/projects/:id/files/* or use DNS rebinding to plant package.json scripts or agent configs, leading to command execution.

HyperFrames before 0.8.73 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Studio server waveform and thumbnail routes that percent-decode paths without containment checks. Unauthenticated attackers, including script in a malicious composition, can send encoded ../ sequences to probe file existence and extract waveform data from files outside the project.

ioBroker.lovelace before 7.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the onCards() request handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read arbitrary files via unsanitized dot-dot segments. Attackers can send crafted requests to the /cards/_static_/, /hacsfiles/, or /local/custom_ui/ routes to read files including ioBroker configuration and stored credentials.

BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to impersonate administrators by abusing a hard-coded default jwt_secret used by AuthJwt. Attackers can forge an HS256 token offline naming user_id 1 with the admin role, send it as access_token_cookie, and gain full administrative access to users, workspaces, knowledge bases and workflows.

ModelScope 1.11.0 to before 1.40.1 contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability in the image-to-3D SyncDreamer pipeline that allows remote attackers to execute code via crafted model configuration. Attackers can publish a model whose syncdreamer.yaml target field makes instantiate_from_config() import and instantiate any class with controlled params, without an allowlist or trust_remote_code check, executing code when victims load it.

Radicale 3.3.0 before 3.8.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inherit group-based rights by reusing group memberships never reset between requests. Attackers can send credential-less requests after a group member logs in to read and write group-shared calendar and address book collections evaluated by the from_file rights backend.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in xmt_parse_mf_field() in loader_xmt.c caused by unchecked cursor advancement when splitting multi-value XMT-A fields. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file opened with MP4Box to make xmt_parse_string() read past the heap buffer and crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an invalid pointer free vulnerability in gf_sg_command_del() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that allows attackers to corrupt the heap via crafted XMT scene files. Attackers can supply an XMT-A file whose command field_ptr references the embedded new_node member, causing free() on an interior address and crashing MP4Box.

Storyden before 1.26.17 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the AccountRemoveRole handler that allows non-administrator users with MANAGE_ROLES to remove administrator roles. Attackers can send DELETE requests to the account roles endpoint to demote other administrators, potentially leaving the instance with no administrator.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_command() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to access freed memory via a dangling command buffer pointer. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file whose Replace command frees a Conditional node, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting the heap.

Phoboslab pl_mpeg through commit c871f2b contains an integer underflow in plm_demux_seek() that allows attackers to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads via crafted MPEG-PS files. Attackers can supply a PES packet with payload under 6 bytes, wrapping the packet->length - 6 loop bound during force_intra seeking to crash applications.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process via ROUTE elements. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file placing a ROUTE element before any scene command creates an access unit, crashing MP4Box during encoding and causing denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying XMT-A elements that define and use the same node identifier. Attackers can craft an XMT scene file processed by MP4Box so xmt_text_content() accesses the freed node, crashing the process and possibly corrupting heap memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in load_xmt_done() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that releases references for duplicate node stack entries. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file encoded with MP4Box to crash the process and potentially corrupt heap memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_new_od_link_from_node() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file with an MFURL object-descriptor link lacking an OD ID and name, crashing MP4Box for denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that frees a node when a DEF attribute names a previously referenced undefined node. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing freed heap memory to be used and crashing the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that leaves dangling MFURL pointers when xmt_node_end() discards nodes. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to access freed heap memory and crash the process.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a use of uninitialized variable vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying duplicate PROTO field names. Attackers can trick a user into opening a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_parse_sf_field() to write through an uninitialized pointer and crash the process.

Flowise 3.1.3 through 3.1.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read MCP server bearer tokens via the GET /api/v1/public-chatflows/:id handler. Attackers can use the leaked mcpServerConfig token on the POST /api/v1/mcp/:chatflowId route to invoke chatflows, bypassing API key protection and consuming the owner's model quota.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying unbalanced command buffer closing elements. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT-A file with MP4Box, causing xmt_node_end() to treat a GF_Command as an SFCommandBuffer and crash the process.

Frappe HR (hrms) before 16.9.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the hrms.api.roster.get_events method that allows authenticated employees to view other employees' leave and shift data by bypassing User Permissions. Attackers with the Employee role can call get_events with empty filters for any date range to retrieve every employee's approved leave applications and shift assignments, including leave types, dates, shift locations and times.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in gf_filter_pid_resolve_file_template_ex() in src/filter_core/filter_pid.c that allows local attackers to write past fixed GF_MAX_PATH stack buffers. Attackers can convince a user to segment a crafted NHML input referencing an overly long media file name with MP4Box -dash to crash the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow in gf_xml_sax_parse_intern() in src/utils/xml_parser.c that causes a heap-based buffer overflow when completing partially buffered entities. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XML or XMT file with MP4Box, overflowing xml_sax_append_string() size arithmetic to corrupt heap memory and crash the process.

This happens because a namespace-scoped issuer that supplies no credentials, or sets only a role, falls back to the controller's own identity.

WPS Limit Login (wps-limit-login) before 1.5.9.5 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass login lockout protections by keying the per-attempt login counter and lockout map on the raw, non-canonicalized IPv6 client address. Attackers controlling a routable IPv6 /64 prefix can send each login attempt from a fresh address within that range, preventing any counter from reaching the lockout threshold and enabling effectively unlimited brute-force password guessing against WordPress accounts.

Effect is a TypeScript framework that consists of several packages that work together to help build TypeScript applications. Prior to 3.22.1, Schema.TemplateLiteral schemas containing at least two Schema.String spans compile each span to the ambiguous lazy wildcard [\s\S]*?. Decoding a non-matching untrusted string causes cubic regular expression backtracking, which can block the JavaScript event loop. The issue affects Schema.decodeUnknown, Schema.decodeUnknownSync, Schema.is, and consumers such as HttpApi and @effect/rpc payload decoding. This issue is fixed in version 3.22.1.

The ICRTouch white-label TouchTakeaway Cordova applications do not implement certificate or public-key pinning for backend HTTPS connections. The applications therefore rely exclusively on the device’s system trust store when validating server certificates.
An attacker who can cause a device to trust an attacker-controlled certificate authority, or who operates through a compromised or improperly issued trusted certificate, may be able to intercept and modify application traffic.

An attacker with access to the POS protocol may be able to specify another employee’s clerk identifier and submit payment-related requests under that identity.

An attacker with network access to the POS socket service may be able to submit a crafted `SAVECONFIG` command and replace or modify terminal configuration data.

ICRTouch Commander administrative interface performs security-sensitive operations through HTTP GET requests and includes an API key in the request query string. The wallet top-up functionality in ICRTouch ByTable and TouchTakeaway does not adequately protect state-changing requests against CSRF. An attacker who convinces an authenticated user to visit a malicious website may cause the user’s browser to submit unauthorized requests to the platform using the user’s active session.

A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to data tampering and information disclosure.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in its command-line diagnostic interface where an attacker could cause OS command injection because user- or configuration-supplied values are incorporated into a command that is interpreted by two successive shell layers in the remote path while being escaped for only one layer. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to code execution, escalation of privileges, information disclosure, data tampering, and denial of service.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in its gateway connection-proxy component where an attacker who can manipulate a sandbox's status metadata could cause the control-plane server to initiate connections to arbitrary internal hosts because the connection target is derived from that metadata and used without validation against the expected address range. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in its gateway-to-sandbox transport where a network attacker positioned on the internal path could intercept credentials and tamper with commands and data because the transport accepts any host key without verification, permitting a machine-in-the-middle to impersonate the sandbox endpoint. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure, data tampering, and code execution.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in L7 REST policy enforcement where a local attacker with low privileges could exploit inconsistent HTTP interpretation by using cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c) over an HTTP CONNECT tunnel to bypass policy restrictions. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in Kubernetes network policy enforcement where a local attacker with low privileges could cause the proxy to attribute network traffic to a different process due to TCP source-port identity confusion, allowing the attacker to bypass process-based network policy restrictions. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in the Kubernetes sandbox SSH authentication configuration where a local attacker with low privileges could obtain sensitive authentication information by accessing an SSH handshake secret stored in a plaintext environment variable and reuse the shared secret to gain unauthorized access to other sandboxes. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure, data tampering, and denial of service.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in the sandbox SSH authentication component where a remote attacker with high privileges could gain unauthorized access to other sandboxes by using an SSH handshake secret shared across sandboxes. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure, data tampering, and denial of service.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in L7 policy enforcement for HTTP CONNECT tunnels where a local attacker with low privileges could cause a protection mechanism failure by using nonstandard HTTP methods to bypass policy restrictions. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in resource-level authorization for create, read, update, and delete operations where an authenticated remote attacker with low privileges could access or modify resources without the required authorization checks. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in the L7 path allowlist enforcement component where a local attacker with low privileges could cause path traversal by using semicolon-dot path sequences to bypass allowlist restrictions. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure, data tampering, and denial of service.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in the network policy hot-reload component where a local attacker with low privileges could bypass updated network policy restrictions through existing L7-inspected tunnels that continue to use the previous policy after a reload. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.
NVIDIA TensorRT for Linux contains a vulnerability where a user could cause an integer overflow issue. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to denial of service and data tampering.

Attackers can supply a crafted filelist input processed by MP4Box with -add, causing gf_props_del_property() to access freed memory and crash the application.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an uninitialized pointer access vulnerability in GetESD() in src/isomedia/track.c that allows attackers to trigger invalid memory reads via crafted MP4 files. Attackers can supply an MP4 with an rvcc box having predefined_rvc_config set to 0 and no meta item index, causing strcmp() on an uninitialized mime_type pointer and crashing MP4Box -add.

GPAC 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in dasher_configure_pid() in src/filters/dasher.c that dereferences ds2->set without checking for NULL. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG-2 TS file processed with MP4Box -dash to disconnect a PID and crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.

Attackers who control values like profile fields or API responses can break out of the template literal to access the page DOM, non-HttpOnly cookies, and the ReactNativeWebView message bridge.

The CeliachiaRL integration component distributed with Farmasimplex uses shared OAuth credentials across multiple customer installations. An attacker who obtains the credentials from one installation could reuse them against services associated with other installations, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information or modification of integration data.

The REV.exe module distributed with Farmasimplex contains embedded OAuth client credentials for integration with the IZS platform. An attacker with access to the executable could extract and reuse the credentials, potentially leading to unauthorized access to integration resources or manipulation of associated information, depending on the privileges granted and authentication controls in place.

Multiple Farmasimplex healthcare integration modules do not properly validate TLS certificates, allowing an attacker who can intercept network traffic to impersonate trusted healthcare services and perform man-in-the-middle attacks, potentially leading to disclosure or modification of sensitive data.

Farmasimplex retrieves a CIP News file over HTTP and executes embedded SQL statements against the local FarmaCIP database with administrative privileges. An attacker able to tamper with network communications or compromise vendor infrastructure can inject arbitrary SQL commands, leading to unauthorized access to, modification or deletion of database contents and potentially operating system command execution.

WP File Manager before 8.0.7 contains a file upload restriction bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to upload arbitrary PHP files by exploiting a misconfigured elFinder connector in file_folder_manager.php where an empty uploadDeny list causes allowPutMime() to unconditionally return true, bypassing the uploadAllow restriction. Attackers can upload a .php file directly or upload it under an allowed filename and then rename it via the rename connector command, achieving remote code execution as the web server user.

Flowise through 3.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to reach internal services by exploiting unpinned DNS validation in checkDenyList(). Attackers can configure a chatflow with Playwright or Puppeteer loaders using a DNS-rebinding domain so headless Chromium fetches internal or cloud metadata endpoints, returning responses as document content.

When using the admin area profile form to change ones profile details *except* the password (so, email or username), the password field in the database is overwritten with the plaintext password. Further login is not possible, so the error is noticeable, but the password is leaked to the database.

Attackers can email the polled fax mailbox with a spoofed authorized From address and use ../ sequences in the filename to create or overwrite web-server-writable files with .pdf/.tif content.

SQLBot 1.10.0 through 1.10.3 fails to apply its PostgreSQL dangerous-function denylist because DS_SPECIFIC_DANGEROUS_FUNCTIONS uses 'postgresql' while lookups use the 'pg' type. Authenticated users can steer LLM-generated SQL past check_sql_read() using pg_read_file, pg_write_file, lo_import or lo_export to read or write files on the database host.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject scripts by supplying unescaped ScalarConfig title values. Attackers controlling title metadata can close the title element with </title> and inject a script tag that executes in the documentation origin for API reference visitors.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in get_scalar_api_reference() that embeds unescaped OpenAPI content inside an inline script element. Attackers can supply an OpenAPI document containing a </script><script> sequence in content or sources to execute scripts in the documentation origin for every user viewing the API reference.

phpMyFAQ 4.0.12 through 4.0.19, 4.1.x before 4.1.12, and 4.2.0 pre-releases before 4.2.0-RC.1 contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in startpage.twig, where top-ten FAQ titles are rendered with Twig's raw filter. Authenticated users with FAQ edit permission can save a question containing a double quote and event handler, which runs script for every start page visitor.

53AIHub before 0.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files by requesting /api/files/:file_id/preview and /api/file-version/:file_body_id without UserTokenAuth. Attackers can enumerate sequential numeric ids to read raw knowledge-base files and stored file versions belonging to any enterprise tenant.

react-native-webview 11.25.1 through 17.1.0 on Android contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows web content to crash the host application via malformed Content-Disposition headers. Attackers can serve a download whose filename* parameter has invalid percent-encoding, triggering an uncaught IllegalArgumentException in URLUtil.parseContentDisposition on the main thread to terminate the app.

Emitter through 3.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows any channel key holder to forge a master key because channel keys use bare XOR Salsa20 encryption without a MAC or signature. Attackers can flip the permissions byte to the master value and present the forged key to the keygen service to mint keys with arbitrary permissions on every channel of the contract.

OpenFunction through 1.2.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in getServingRun that allows users permitted to create Serving resources to crash the operator by omitting the triggers section. Attackers can submit a Serving with nil Spec.Triggers to crash-loop the controller-manager, halting Function and Serving reconciliation cluster-wide until the object is deleted.

OpenFunction through 1.2.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows namespace tenants to create privileged host-access pods by supplying unrestricted PodSpec templates in Function and Serving resources. Attackers with only Function or Serving create permissions can set privileged, hostNetwork, hostPID, or hostPath fields to mount the worker node's root filesystem and escalate to node access.

Xibo CMS before 4.5.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other DataSets' RSS feeds by pairing their own DataSet id with a foreign RSS id. Attackers with dataset.modify permission can read, edit, or delete feeds and steal PSKs, then use the unauthenticated /rss/{psk} endpoint to exfiltrate victim DataSet rows.

Rootways Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2 before 4.1.5 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Apple Pay merchant validation controller. Attackers can supply file://, gopher://, or dict:// URLs in the validationUrl parameter to read app/etc/env.php credentials and encryption keys or reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in coap_remove_observer_by_uri() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read past the supplied URI buffer. Attackers can send a CoAP GET Observe request with a Uri-Path shorter than an existing observer's URL, causing memcmp with strlen to read beyond the non-NUL-terminated buffer.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds access vulnerability in buffer_reclaim() and domain_set_free() in mpl.c that iterate the seed_set array one element past its end. Remote attackers can flood MPL multicast messages to fill the buffered message set, triggering out-of-bounds reads and writes of adjacent static memory that cause memory corruption or a crash.

Weblate 2026.11 through 2026.11.2 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the GET /api/tasks/{pk}/ endpoint that exposes unredacted repository error messages. Authenticated project members lacking vcs.view permission can poll failing repository tasks to obtain RepositoryCommandError text revealing upstream repository URLs, filesystem paths, and host names.

Bludit is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the page deletion functionality. An authenticated user with the Author role can set the UUID field of their own page to contain path traversal sequences (.. and path separators), which are saved without proper validation. When the page is deleted, Pages::delete() passes the path constructed from this UUID to Filesystem::deleteRecursive() without verifying that it still points to an allowed directory, allowing the attacker to delete any files, even not belonging to them. Critically, it is possible to delete admin pages and render the site unusable.

The WP Abstracts plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.6. This is due to a missing capability check on the wpabs_save_regform AJAX action and the use of a static, frontend-exposed nonce that allows any authenticated user to persist attacker-controlled form schemas with arbitrary wpSync mappings that are later used as user meta keys in the wpabstracts_sync_wpfields function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to administrator.

When changing the settings of a scheduled export, no permission checks are done to see whether the user making the change has access to the exporter after the change. This way, an attacker with access to change organizer settings and e.g. access to all orders could change the export to refer to gift cards instead, even if they do not have access to gift cards.




The fix for this is technically a breaking API change, since changing the export type of existing scheduled exports is no longer allowed, but we don't expect this to affect any typical API usage.

These HTTP calls are made with wp_remote_get, not wp_safe_remote_get, and therefore allow SSRF with body extraction. Exploiting this requires sufficient WordPress permissions to create or modify pages.

This could allow a skilled attacker with access to at least some of the tokens to predict the value of other tokens more easily.




pretixSCAN is usually used on local networks and the level of exposure heavily depends on the structure of that network. If you want to be extra careful, it might make sense to reconnect your devices to the proxy after the update.

This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to the exposure of internal hospital operational statistics through data structure embedded in the HTML response of the login page. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by accessing the affected login page and extracting the returned HTML content.

This vulnerability exists in e-Sushrut HMIS due to insufficient authentication and session validation in the dashboard functionality. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted HTTP requests to the affected endpoint.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to gain unauthorized access to the dashboard information associated with the targeted healthcare organization.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 processes XML external entities in software repository files. An attacker able to supply or modify the repository files received by the server can read files accessible to the N-central service account or cause the server to make outbound requests.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not validate version values and download locations in software update metadata. An attacker able to supply or modify the update metadata received by the server can write files outside the download directory and execute code as the N-central service account.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not verify that an action response received over XMPP originates from the appliance the request was sent to. An attacker with the credentials of one appliance can forge responses on behalf of another appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not validate connection targets in the Report Manager and Data Export settings. An authenticated attacker can cause the server to connect to arbitrary hosts, including loopback and internal addresses, and can use the responses to probe internal network services.

The custom service import in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 processes XML external entities. An authenticated attacker can upload a crafted service definition to read files accessible to the N-central service account or cause the server to make outbound requests.

The test email delivery function in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not check permissions, lacks CSRF protection, and passes sender and recipient values to the mail program without neutralising option characters. An authenticated attacker can inject arguments into the mail command executed on the server.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 checks only a view permission for ServerII2 operations that write device execution configuration. An authenticated user with view-only access to a device can set configuration that the Windows agent on that device acts on.

Multiple ServerUI and ServerUI2 SOAP operations in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 do not verify the caller's session, permissions or customer scope. A remote attacker, in some cases without authentication, can read device and patch data, test passwords of user accounts, send messages to managed agents, and modify device and service settings belonging to other customers.

The password reset function in N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 returns distinguishable responses for valid and invalid accounts. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can enumerate the email addresses of valid user accounts.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerII2 remoteControlMSPAStartEndTimeSubmit operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can alter the recorded state and times of Take Control remote control tasks and the associated audit log entries.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the MaintActionGet operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can read and cancel the pending maintenance actions of any appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerMMS2 AssetDiscoSimplifiedInfoSubmit operation. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can overwrite the asset data recorded for any appliance.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 allows the repositoryItemGet operation to be called without authentication. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who knows a policy identifier can download the Automation Manager policy of any customer, including embedded scripts and parameter values.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not authenticate callers of the ServerMMS2 RemoteExecutionTaskSubmit operation or verify task ownership. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can submit forged results for remote execution tasks belonging to any customer.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 does not neutralise control characters in an Audit Export setting before writing it to the system logging configuration. An authenticated attacker with product administrator privileges can inject configuration and execute commands as root on the N-central server.

N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 uses a predictable credential to authenticate appliances to an agent-facing API. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who knows or guesses an appliance identifier can obtain a valid appliance token and session and impersonate that appliance.

The RSS widget of the dashboard allows backend users to configure the URL of the RSS feed in the widget settings. The URL was fetched by the server without restricting the target host. Backend users with access to the dashboard could therefore make the server send HTTP requests to arbitrary hosts, including internal network services and cloud metadata endpoints, which are not reachable from the outside.

The file dump controller (eID=dumpFile) delivers files, file references and processed files identified by their uid, protected by a token. The token only covered the uid value, but not the type of the requested resource. A valid token issued for a file could therefore be reused to request a file reference or a processed file with the same uid. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could download files, for example from non-public storages, for which no token had been issued.
